title: Chocolate and salted caramel tart
subtitle: a rich dark chocolate ganache tart on a layer of salted caramel
excerpt: This tart has three layers: a crisp chocolate shortcrust case, a layer of salted caramel, and a smooth dark chocolate ganache on top. The filling is set by chilling rather than baking once the case is filled. Each component is straightforward on its own; the skill is in the assembly. Serve in small slices: it is very rich.
sourceNotes: Chocolate and salted caramel tart, a contemporary British patisserie classic from the early 2000s. Method from standard British and French patisserie practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A smooth emulsion of chocolate and hot cream, poured as a glaze or set as a filling. For a tart, a 1:1 ratio of cream to chocolate gives a firm but yielding texture.
A caramel made from sugar, butter, and cream, finished with flaky sea salt. The salt enhances the bitter-sweet caramel flavour and gives a savoury contrast.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The completed tart keeps refrigerated for up to 3 days. Remove from the fridge 30 minutes before serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: 180°C fan / 200°C conventional / gas 6 for the pastry

content.text: layer goes into the tart case first, while still warm and pourable. It sets as the

cools to pouring temperature. The two layers must be added at the right moment: the caramel while warm enough to flow, and the ganache once it has cooled to just above setting point so it does not melt the caramel. Use a 1:1 ratio of cream to chocolate for the ganache, which is richer than a truffle ganache but still pourable.
Rub together the flour, cocoa, icing sugar, and cold butter to fine crumbs. Stir in the egg yolk and enough cold water (about 2 tablespoons) to bring the pastry together. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Blind-bake for 15 minutes, then remove the beans and bake for 5 more minutes. Cool completely.

Melt the caster sugar in a dry pan over medium heat until a deep amber caramel. Stir in the warm cream carefully (it will bubble vigorously), then stir in the butter and flaky salt. Pour into the cooled pastry case and leave to set for 30 minutes until just firm.

Pour the 200 ml of cream over the chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Leave for 2 minutes, then stir from the centre until a smooth ganache forms. Cool to about 35°C (warm but not hot) before pouring over the caramel layer.
Smooth the surface gently and refrigerate for at least 3 hours until fully set. Remove from the fridge 30 minutes before serving and cut with a hot, dry knife.

attrs.problem: Ganache melts the caramel when poured
attrs.avoid: Avoid pouring the ganache while it is still too hot; it should feel barely warm on the back of your hand.
attrs.fix: Let the ganache cool to 30 to 35°C before pouring. If it sets too thick to pour, warm very briefly over a bowl of hot water.

attrs.avoid: Avoid stirring the caramel once the sugar is melting.
attrs.fix: Heat sugar in a clean, dry pan without stirring, swirling gently instead. Discard crystallised caramel and start again.
